prerequisites: Handling of different coordinate systems and vector algebra

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the movement of water through pressure conduits (pipes), as an introduction and basis for the analysis of piping systems.
Know and understand the movement of water in open conduits (free regime movement or open channels).
Acquire the necessary skill to solve practical problems.

Acquire the necessary knowledge to understand the operation, study, and construction of machinery to be used in hydraulic works (turbomachinery in general, pumping installations, and hydraulic turbines) that the Mechanical Engineer must build and install in their professional practice.

Knowledge and understanding of the behavior of fluids in general, and water in particular, in their movement through pressure conduits (pipes) or free regime conduits (channels), as well as their results and consequences.
Knowledge and understanding of the behavior of hydraulic machines (pumps and hydraulic turbines), used in the various hydraulic works that can be built, as well as their results and consequences.

Knowledge and understanding of the applicability of Hydraulic Machinery to the practical reality of Mechanical Engineering to achieve an adequate development of the capacities of Application, Analysis and Valuation of the knowledge acquired in the practical context required by their future professional practice.

Development of Interpretation and Synthesis capabilities of the information provided by the bibliography, reduced models and hydraulic works and projects carried out; thanks to the global knowledge of the subject and its applicability.
Learning and correct use of elementary hydraulic terminology, for access and understanding of basic bibliography and correct expression of acquired knowledge.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for searching for sustainable engineering solutions.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES: Continuity Theorem. Bernoulli's Theorem. Generalization of Bernoulli's Theorem. Momentum Theorem.

CONTINUOUS HEAD LOSSES, DUE TO FRICTION: General Darcy-Weisbach law. Friction coefficient. Moody diagram. Hydraulic calculation of pipes. Empirical formulas: Chezy's Formula. Manning's Formula. Other empirical formulas.
LOCALIZED HEAD LOSSES: General expression. Elbows and valves. Constrictions. Enlargements.

PIPE SYSTEMS AND NETWORK MODELS: Elementary networks: Confluences, bifurcations, parallel pipes. Branched networks and reticulated networks. Design flows. Network calculation. Mathematical models applied to network calculation: practical applications, software programs.
POWER OF A FLUID FLOW: Pumping, general scheme and pump power, limitations of suction head. Turbines, general scheme and power.
VARIABLE FLOW IN CONDUITS: Mass oscillation and water hammer phenomena. General equations of water hammer. Approximate methods for solving the water hammer phenomenon. Surge tanks.
TURBOMACHINERY: Fundamentals and definition. Classification. Energy losses, powers and efficiencies. Elementary theory of turbomachinery. Similarity in turbomachinery.

HYDRAULIC PUMPS: Introduction. Classification of pumps. Centrifugal pump. Characteristic curves of pumps. Pump efficiency according to specific speed and size. Proportions and design factors. Cavitation in pumps. Coupling of pumps to the network (in parallel and in series).

HYDRAULIC TURBINES: Power plants, types and classification of hydroelectric power plants. Most common types of hydraulic turbines. Impulse turbines (Pelton turbines). Reaction turbines (Francis turbine, Double Francis turbine, Propeller turbines, Kaplan turbines, Bulb turbines, Deriaz turbines). Specific speed and similarity in turbines. Cavitation in turbines. Preliminary design of turbines. Turbine efficiency. Turbine control, remote control.
FREE REGIME CHARACTERISTICS AND CLASSIFICATION: Channels. Geometry of channels. Influence of gravity. Froude number. Types of regime: Slow regime, Critical regime, Rapid regime.

TOTAL ENERGY AND SPECIFIC ENERGY: Total energy. Particularizations of the continuity and dynamics equations. Longitudinal and transversal velocity distribution. Pressure distribution. Specific energy: study of different situations.
HYDRAULIC JUMP: Energy dissipator. Definition and conjugate depths. Resolution. Calculation of energy loss and jump length.

UNIFORM REGIME: Particularization of Bernoulli's Theorem. Application of Manning's Formula. Capacity curves or flow curves in simple sections. Flow in compound sections. Applications: gauging stations. Analogy with natural compound sections, rivers: Central channel and floodplains.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving exercises with active student participation
Personal study of theory and problems/practices
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, it is essential to obtain at least 4 out of 10 in the final written exam to average the grades. Positive aspects such as class participation, motivation, and interest in the subject will also be valued.
